declared.title: The pursuit of happiness can be lonely.

population: a 2-week diary study and a lab experiment; sample sizes and country not given in the abstract

findings.text: People led to value happiness felt lonelier than controls, by their own report and by a hormone (progesterone)

support.sentence: Study 2 provides an experimental manipulation of valuing happiness and demonstrates that inducing people to value happiness leads to relatively greater loneliness, as measured by self-reports and a hormonal index (progesterone).

findings.text: Over two weeks of diaries, the more people valued happiness, the lonelier they felt day to day

support.sentence: Study 1 suggests that the more people value happiness, the lonelier they feel on a daily basis (assessed over 2 weeks with diaries).

limits: loneliness, not happiness: another negative experience
sample sizes not given in the abstract (full text not read)
same lab as Mauss 2011; no replication found (2026-11-22)
